authority_basis.claim_scope: Net external force equals mass times acceleration for constant mass, resolved consistently by axis.

concepts.statement: Newton's second law applies to the vector sum of external forces on the selected system, not to any one force in isolation.
concepts.why_required: The law connects the complete external interaction model to system acceleration.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: A single named force may be incorrectly equated to ma while other external forces are ignored.

symbols.name: signed net external force on x axis
signed net external force on y axis

model_conditions.condition: All forces and acceleration components refer to the same selected system and the same axis convention.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Newton's second law is a vector statement for one system, so mixed-system or mixed-axis terms are invalid.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The equations combine quantities that do not belong to one physical model.

model_conditions.condition: The analysed system has constant mass over the interval modelled by sum(F)=ma.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The simple constant-mass form is being used rather than the general momentum equation.

representations.semantic_geometry: A complete selected-system FBD is overlaid with declared coordinate axes so each external force can be resolved into signed components feeding the axis-wise Newton equations.
must_not_imply: different axis equations may use different system boundaries
representations.verification_method: Reconstruct the net-force vector from signed components and compare its direction with the acceleration vector.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Select the system and construct a complete FBD before writing any Newton equation.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The equation can omit external forces or include forces on other bodies.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Choose axes and resolve forces only after the physical FBD is complete.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Component signs and force projections can be inconsistent.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Write net-force equations axis-wise for the same system and same declared axes.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A single force may be equated to ma or terms from different systems can be mixed.

required_transformations.description: Translate each external force on the complete FBD into signed components under one declared axis convention.
Sum force components axis-wise and equate each net component to the corresponding acceleration component for the same system.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Any named force can be set equal to ma without summing all external forces.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Many simple one-force examples collapse net force to a single force and hide the vector-sum requirement.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A block pulled horizontally while friction acts has acceleration determined by pull minus friction, not by either force alone.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Use a complete FBD with all external forces before showing the signed component sum.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Start from the complete FBD and form the signed net force on each axis.
misconceptions.verification: Substitute all signed force components and confirm the resultant net-force direction matches the acceleration direction.

problem_families.name: Single-body Newton-II dynamics
problem_families.first_technical_move: Draw the complete FBD before resolving forces into the chosen axes.
fatal_errors: setting one force equal to ma

problem_families.name: Dynamics on an inclined plane
problem_families.first_technical_move: Choose axes parallel and perpendicular to the incline only after the FBD is physically complete.
fatal_errors: resolving gravity with inconsistent angle reference

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the FBD-before-equation invariant from Newton II.
